changes.summary: Declared explicit resource limits and rootless capabilities in the portable recipe build contract.
changes.details: The recipe now carries every author-selectable Podman build input through the signed Controller-to-agent request, including a bounded capability list that defaults to empty. The agent drops all capabilities before adding only declared allowlisted entries inside Podman's rootless user namespace; host privilege, devices, mounts, sockets, security options, storage, cgroups, and generated image identity remain fixed platform policy.

changes.summary: Declared explicit recipe alignment metadata; no runtime behavior changed.
Restricted public build egress to hosts used during Dockerfile execution.
changes.details: Removed nvcr.io because digest-pinned base images are fetched through the separate verified base-image transfer and the build runs with pull disabled.

changes.summary: Identified the official BF16 Diffusers path as a quality-reference variant.
changes.details: Published its exact single-Spark admission envelopes and directs operators to Lightning for latency or FP8mixed ComfyUI for additional headroom. Candidate qualification is unchanged.

changes.summary: Added typed artifact input and output slot contracts.
changes.details: Declared separate prompt and one-or-two-reference image slots plus the exact edited-PNG output.

changes.summary: Added one bounded UTF-8 prompt file to the existing one-or-two-image input contract.
Rejects missing, extra, invalid, or oversized prompt and image inputs before model loading.
Declared the complete recipe contract installable without changing Candidate qualification.
changes.details: The execution contract was already structurally complete; this release makes it available for explicit operator installation while physical build and Spark acceptance remain separate.

changes.summary: Initial reviewed catalog release of Qwen Image Edit 2511 Diffusers single Spark.
Bound the legacy Qwen Image Edit candidate to the corrected adapter digest.
Recovered the first public legacy revision from before semantic release tracking.
